name: bitblocks-bsv402-vectors
description: Test vectors for a server taking BRC-121 (Simple 402 Payments): a BRC-29 output in Atomic BEEF, sent in the x-bsv-* headers, checked against the server's own headers and node. Each says what the server should answer.
versioning: v0 until a real wallet's payment is in it; then v1. Within a version, a vector's id, bytes and expected outcome stay as they are, except to correct a mistake.

basis.derivation: test/support/fixtures/brc/bsv402_brc29_sdk.json in the bitblocks repo: @bsv/sdk 4.1.2's keys for these labels

claim: These vectors cover what a server checks before it serves a paid request: the headers, the time, the BEEF, the output and its key, the amount, the proof against headers, the claim and the node's answer. The transactions are unsigned: a real node would refuse them, so each vector names what the stubbed node answers.
tried_against: Bitblocks.Payments.Bsv402, and the derivation against @bsv/sdk 4.1.2. No live wallet yet. Nothing in this file says any wallet or server conforms to it.
how_to_use: Take server.identity_private_key as your identity key, price_sats as your price and now_ms as your clock.
Treat every entry in headers as a header you hold, verified and on the best chain, and no others. They are made up: rely on merkleroot alone.
Before a vector, treat each txid in claimed as already taken for the request beside it.
Send the vector's payment headers with its request, and have your node answer as node says: accept, already_known, unreachable, or reject:<reason>.
Compare your status and outcome with expected. reason is the name Bitblocks uses, so yours may differ.

derivation.output: P2PKH to the BRC-42 child of the server's key for that invoice, with the sender's key as counterparty

outcomes.accepted: Served: the payment checks, is claimed, and the node took it.
outcomes.reserved: Served again: the same payment for the same request, already claimed; no new claim.
outcomes.refused: Not served. status says how: 402 with the terms again, 413 too large, 503 try again.

vectors.case: One output of exactly the price, its coin proven.
One sat more than the price: at least the price is what BRC-121 asks.
P2PKH to the key derived for another server.
x-bsv-time a second off the time the key was derived for.
Its txid already bought another request.
Its txid already bought this same request: served again, with no new claim.
The coin's BUMP climbs to a root that isn't the header's at that height.
The coin's BUMP names a height with no header.
BEEF V1 without the Atomic prefix (BRC-95).
Our node refuses it, as a double spend.
Our node doesn't answer: nothing is taken.
Our node already has it (the wallet broadcast it first).
A BEEF over max_beef_bytes: its coin carries 12000 bytes of data.

changes.change: Added keyed: a caller with an API key past its own budget. The vectors before it are unchanged.

Added keyed-unbudgeted: a key holding the unbudgeted scope has no budget, so it is served past its requests_per_minute, with no x-ratelimit-* headers. api_key.scopes appears on that vector only. The vectors before it are unchanged.

keyed_how_to_use: These run through the server's HTTP front, not the verifier alone: register api_key.token (when registered is true) as a key of requests_per_minute, and make spent requests with it, within the minute, before the vector's own.
Then send request with request_headers and, when payment isn't null, the payment headers, under the same clock, headers and node as the vectors above.
Compare status, each entry in expected.headers exactly, that each of headers_present is there and each of headers_absent isn't, and that the JSON body holds every field in expected.body.

outcome served or accepted: within the key's budget or paid; a paid request isn't counted against the key's budget. payment_required: past it, the terms given. refused: a payment refused (402 with the terms again), or a key refused (401, and no terms, since a payment can't mend a bad key).

When api_key.scopes is there, register the key holding those scopes. unbudgeted: the key has no rate budget, so it is never refused for its rate or offered a payment, and its responses carry no x-ratelimit-* headers.

keyed.case: A key within its budget: served free, counted against the key.
A key past its budget, no payment: a 402 with BRC-121's terms, where it was a 429.
A key past its budget, paying: served, with what was paid, outside the key's budget.
A key past its budget, its payment's txid already bought another request.
An unknown key with a payment: a 401, never a 402; the payment isn't read.
A key holding the unbudgeted scope, well past its requests_per_minute: served free, never a 429 or a 402, and no x-ratelimit-* headers, since there is no limit to report.
